source_read: PDF (online-first, J Addict Med vol. 00), pp. 1–11 (all pages read; Table 1, Table 2 and Figures 1–3 checked on pages rendered at 110 dpi; supplemental digital content not available in the PDF and not read)

claims.overstatement: Two parts of the statement are not supported by this source. (1) 'About 0.3 to 0.7 SD for most domains': in Cao et al. domain estimates run from −0.42 to −1.09, and 6 of 13 exceed 0.7 in magnitude (visuospatial −1.09, shifting −0.86, self-reported impulsivity −0.86, planning −0.82, verbal learning and memory −0.79, processing speed −0.74). (2) 'Largest for learning and memory': here verbal learning and memory ranks fifth, behind visuospatial, shifting, self-reported impulsivity and planning. The authors call the domain differences non-significant and descriptive. Also, 'there is evidence of publication bias' does not hold for this source's overall estimate (Egger P=0.32, trim-and-fill found no missing studies), though 4 domains showed a signal at P<0.10.
claims.note: Numbers from this source checked. 68 studies, 5244 vs 3801 (p. 6). Overall g −0.68, 95% CI −0.77 to −0.58 (text and abstract; Figure 2 prints −0.59), prediction interval −1.58 to 0.22 (p. 6). The pooled estimate includes self-report impulsivity questionnaires (13 domains, all 242 effect sizes; Methods p. 2, Figure 2 p. 8), so it is not purely a performance-test estimate. The domain omnibus test is printed as F(12, 140.1)=2.07, P=0.10. From that F and df I get p≈0.023, while the other two omnibus tests (comorbidity, abstinence phases) match their printed p-values. The paper says FDR correction was applied to omnibus tests (p. 4) but does not say this p is adjusted. Education 9.94 vs 11.33 years supports the education sentence. Weighted mean abstinence 248 days, with 50 of the 57 studies reporting abstinence under 12 months, is compatible with 'mostly within the first months'.

anchors.extracted: 68 independent studies (64 publications), 242 effect sizes, 9045 participants: 5244 with methamphetamine use disorder, 3801 healthy controls; users 87.2% male; education 9.94 vs 11.33 years; abstinence 4.2–971 days, weighted mean 248.2; mean NOS 6.25, 51.5% of studies rated high quality.

anchors.locator: Results › Cognitive Impairment by Domain in MUD
anchors.extracted: Omnibus between-domain test printed as F(12, 140.1)=2.07, P=0.10; authors treat domain estimates as descriptive. My recomputation from the printed F and df gives p≈0.023.

anchors.locator: Results › Sensitivity Analyses and Publication Bias; Table 2
anchors.extracted: Overall: funnel plot without substantial asymmetry, Egger z=−1.00, P=0.32; trim-and-fill adjusted g −0.65. Domain-level Egger P<0.10 in 4 domains: verbal learning and memory 0.005, working memory <0.001, shifting 0.055, self-reported impulsivity 0.066. Sensitivity estimates −0.62 to −0.72.

Polysubstance use and psychiatric comorbidity included by design; impulsivity measured by self-report and tasks as separate domains; testing within 48 hours of last use or without documented abstinence excluded.

claims.note: Phase estimates checked: −0.70 (N=15), −0.63 (N=35), −0.88 (N=7), F(2, 14.9)=1.20, P=0.33 (my recomputation from F and df gives 0.33). 'Few studies beyond a year' matches the paper's 10.3% (7 of 68). The 7 long-abstinence studies include four large samples (326–567 users) per Table 1, so that stratum is dominated by a few cohorts; the authors attribute its larger estimate to sample selection. The exploratory decision-making spline showed an unadjusted nonlinear pattern (p. 7), a minor qualifier.

anchors.locator: Results › Abstinence Duration and Cognitive Remission › Phase-stratified Subgroup Analysis
anchors.extracted: Under 1 month g −0.70 (15 studies), 1–12 months −0.63 (35), over 12 months −0.88 (7); omnibus F(2, 14.9)=1.20, P=0.33. Attention and verbal learning/memory showed no trend across phases (both P>0.30).

anchors.locator: Results › Restricted Cubic Spline Analysis; Figure 3 (p. 9)
anchors.extracted: Inhibitory control (17 studies, 7–265 days): linear and nonlinear P=0.41; self-reported impulsivity (21 studies, 23–280 days): P=0.64 and 0.74. Exploratory models: 4 of 5 domains flat; decision-making nonlinear, unadjusted.
Only 10.3% of studies reported outcomes beyond 12 months; spline estimates reliable only for the first 9 months; the 1–3-year window unexamined.
The authors state these cross-sectional estimates should not be read as individual-level remission trajectories.

key_findings.correction: Figure 2 (p. 8) prints the upper CI as −0.59; text and abstract give −0.58.

Content correct. 'Methods, Outcomes' is on p. 2 (right column), not p. 4 (p. 4 has the domain-coding section). The pooling of all 242 effect sizes including self-reported impulsivity is shown in Figure 2 (p. 8). Pages should read pp. 2, 7–8.
Add: the printed omnibus P=0.10 does not match F(12, 140.1)=2.07, which gives p≈0.023 unless the value is FDR-adjusted (not stated).
The education result is reported with age and duration of use as 'all P ≥ .30' (p. 6); values are in the supplement.
Also shifting (P=0.055) and self-reported impulsivity (P=0.066) were below 0.10 (Table 2).

reporting_issues.note: Upgrade rule stated in Methods › Certainty of Evidence (p. 6); applied to 4 domains (Table 2 footnote, p. 7).

risk_of_bias.note: Moderate confidence is provisional. The excluded-studies list (a critical AMSTAR 2 item) is in an unread supplement; if it is absent the rating falls to low. The possible sample overlap noted below would also bear on 'appropriate meta-analytic methods'.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial agreed. Also the Introduction frames deficits as produced by methamphetamine exposure and as a well-established consequence of the disorder (p. 1), and the Conclusions call the impairment 'clinically significant' (p. 10) without normative or functional data.

missed: Reporting issue: the domain omnibus test F(12, 140.1)=2.07 corresponds to p≈0.023, not the printed P=0.10 (p. 6). The paper's statement that domains did not differ, and its reading of impairment as 'generalized', may depend on an unstated adjustment.

Possible overlapping samples counted as independent studies (Table 1, pp. 3–4): Fitzpatrick et al. 2020 and 2021 (both 108 users/50 controls, 81/38 men, near-identical age and education); Wang et al. 2024 and Zhou et al. 2024 (46/44 vs 45/43, ages 31.4/26 and education 11.5 in both); Luo et al. 2024 (S4 and S59: 102/51 vs 96/46, near-identical age, abstinence and years of use). This cannot be verified without the primary papers. If confirmed, '68 independent studies' overstates independence.

The over-12-month abstinence stratum (7 studies) includes four large samples of 326–567 users (Chen 2022, Jiang 2022, Jiang 2025, Tian 2022; Table 1), so the −0.88 estimate rests heavily on a few cohorts.
Minor: the Discussion says the visuospatial prediction interval crosses zero (p. 9), while Table 2 prints it as −2.17 to −0.00 without the crossing-zero mark (p. 7).

For the encyclopedia's cognition claim: this source's domain profile (largest visuospatial, shifting, self-reported impulsivity, planning) contradicts 'largest for learning and memory', and 6 of 13 domains exceed 0.7 SD.
